summaryZh: 本文是AgriTechNZ的月度通讯，涵盖多个农业科技领域的重要动态：Bay of Plenty农业科技活动回顾、牧场系统国际网络研讨会系列、evokeAG 2027新西兰代表团招募、新一届执行委员会选举结果、MACSO五周年里程碑，以及多家农业科技公司的高管任命。文章强调行业正从技术验证转向商业化落地，人才引进和跨区域合作成为关键趋势。
featuredReason: 本文虽为行业通讯综合内容，但涵盖了智慧畜牧领域的关键趋势：从技术验证到商业化落地的转变、AI动物健康公司MACSO的全球化部署、以及多家畜牧科技企业（Bovonic、Agovor）引入高级运营人才推动规模化。对于关注畜牧科技商业化路径和行业生态建设的从业者具有参考价值。
contentFull:
The people and connections shaping agritech

 
 
 Newsletter

 

 

 

 
 

 
 
 

 

In August, we brought the Bay of Plenty agritech community together for Agritech Unleashed in Tauranga. Founders, growers, tech companies, researchers, investors and industry leaders filled the room, and the region’s appetite to turn innovation into on-farm and commercial results was clear from the first session.

The programme was built to provoke, not reassure. Jarred Mair, Chief Insight Officer Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI), opened on the global forces reshaping our farming systems. Steve Saunders of Yamaha Agriculture and Dr Sandhya Sriram of Sprout Agritech ran a master class in building partnerships at global scale. Workshops took the day from discussion into working material, exploring digital twins with Kar Mun Chooi of the Bioeconomy Science Institute, and the horticulture data ecosystem with Peter McHannigan and Kathryn Mountain of Rush Digital.

The day was long and the energy held, largely because people were willing to say difficult things in front of their peers. Growers have stopped funding unproven technology. Reliability and service now decide what gets bought. And much of what the room first described as a technology problem turned out to be a matching problem: people with a problem worth solving and people able to solve it, not finding each other early enough or on honest enough terms.

That is the argument for gathering in place. These events are not a showcase. They are where the sector tests its own assumptions in a room small enough that nobody can hide behind a slide, and where relationships form that carry the work forward long after the day ends. Read the full report here.Next, we head south. Agritech Unleashed Otago in Dunedin on 12 November closes the 2026 series, with livestock and pastoral systems as the context. The questions are the same and the answers will not be. What does shared progress look like when the context is animals on the land, and how do genetics, data, observation and on-farm decisions move together rather than separately?

Kicking off with a networking event the evening before, we hope some of you can join us early. We look forward to seeing the ecosystem come together for our last event of the year. Building up to it, we are running a three-part international webinar series on pasture and rangeland systems with partners in Australia, Colorado and Wyoming… some global contexts to inspire local insights. More on that below.

New International Webinar Series: Global Innovation in Pasture and Rangeland Systems

AgriTech New Zealand is joining partners in Australia, Colorado and Wyoming for a three-part series on how innovation can strengthen pasture and rangeland systems.

Four regions, four sets of constraints, and a great deal of shared ground. Farmers, ranchers, agritech leaders, researchers, investors, and regional development organisations will talk practically about what is working and what is not: on-farm resilience, technology adoption/adaptation, investment, policy, and the partnerships needed to take promising ideas past the pilot stage.

The sessions are free and run from late September to late October. They also serve as deliberate preparation for Dunedin. The questions raised here about grazing systems, data, adoption, and ecosystem dynamics are the questions we will put on stage in November, with the benefit of an international read with near peers first.

Each webinar includes a live audience Q&A. When you register, you can submit a burning question on the challenges, innovations or collaboration opportunities shaping pasture and rangeland systems. Those questions will help guide the discussion and show us where stronger international connections and shared learning could lead to practical next steps. Saddle up, and plant your question!

Register here.

evokeAG 2027: Register your interest

Australia is the natural next market for many New Zealand agritech companies, and evokeAG brings together the people who can help make that move happen: agribusiness leaders, government agencies, startups, researchers, producers and investors from across the Asia-Pacific.

It is also more than a market. Climate pressures and customers are shared across the region, and with neighbours like Singapore, the relationship runs deeper again: their food security needs and our innovation capability rely on each other. Add better capital flow across the region, and there is a strong case for developing a common position rather than each of us doing it alone. 

As the region’s largest agrifood tech event, evokeAG brings together more than 1,500 people over two days. Joining the New Zealand delegation is a practical way to build the connections, visibility and local understanding needed to enter and grow in Australia.

Register your interest to join the New Zealand delegation (collaboratively convened by Sprout Agritech, National Fieldays Society and NZTE). Participants receive:

A discounted international event ticket 

Coordinated support and warm introductions on the ground

Connections to relevant government agencies

Visibility through AgriFutures’ GrowAG platform before and after the event

Register your interest to be part of the delegation here.

Annual Meeting Recap: welcoming our new Executive Council

Thank you to everyone who joined our Annual Meeting on 13 August. Alongside the annual reflection and the financial report, members elected the incoming Executive Council. The council sets our direction and carries the membership’s voice, so it is worth introducing them properly. 

Congratulations to Chelsea Hirst (NZ Product Accelerator) and Grant Kay (LIC), who join the Executive Council following the election. We again had a strong field across the categories this year and a properly contested vote… possibly a warm-up act for November! And a good problem for an industry body to have. 

Our thanks to Tammy Lemire (Pamu) and Elliot Mercer (Agnition), who step down after generously giving their time, networks, and judgement. Both leave the organisation in better shape than they found it, and we look forward to staying connected.The Executive Council for the year ahead:

Major corporate: Grant Kay (LIC), Tui Williams (Fonterra)

Other corporate: Chelsea Hirst, Deputy-Chair (NZ Product Accelerator), Tom Woutersen (Halter)

Start-ups and SME: Brenna Townshend, Chair (Trev), Sophie Stanley (Levno)

Government: Chris Kerr (MPI)

Independent: Ruth Leary (AgriZero)

The categories matter here. Council members are elected to represent a part of the membership, not the interests of the organisation that employs them. A major corporate seat brings the perspective of every large agribusiness in our membership, and the start-up seats speak for the whole cohort of early-stage companies, not just their own. It is a real ask of people, and our council members take it seriously.

That is where our strength comes from. The work these eight do between meetings, and the breadth of the membership behind them, gives us standing when we speak on behalf of the sector. It only holds if members keep putting their hands up. Thank you for continuing to do so.

Member Spotlight: Macso celebrates 5 years

Congratulations to MACSO, which just celebrated its fifth birthday. Founded with a bold ambition to transform animal health through AI, MACSO is now moving from breakthrough technology to commercial deployment at global scale.

This milestone reflects the contribution of MACSO’s team, customers, partners, investors, advisers and supporters. As the company enters its next chapter, its progress is a strong example of New Zealand agritech translating ambitious innovation into international impact.

Movers & Shakers

There is a quiet signal in the sector right now that says a lot about where we have got to. Founders who have proven their product are bringing in senior operators to help them scale, and doing it early enough to matter.

At Bovonic, founder Liam Kampshof and his Board have appointed Chris Morgan as General Manager, bringing more than 40 years of experience in the New Zealand dairy industry to a company moving from proving its technology, to selling it at volume.

At Agovor, co-founders Richard Beaumont and Simon Carroll have Michael Riley in the CEO seat, a seasoned agtech operator with scaling and governance experience across Australia and New Zealand.

Different companies, different technologies, same instinct. The skills that get a product to market are not always the skills that scale a business, and both sets of founders have gone looking for people who have done it before. That’s a mark of both confidence and ambition.

It also says something about the sector’s pull. Experienced operators with options are choosing agritech, and choosing it here. Talent attracts talent, and each appointment makes the next one easier to land. Congratulations to Liam, Richard and Simon, and welcome to Chris and Michael.

Upcoming Events

22 Sep: World Agri-Tech Innovation Summit 2026

23 – 25 Sep: Emergent Leaders for Change Programme

28-29 Sep: Red Meat Sector Conference

29 Sep: International Webinar Series: Global Innovation in Pasture and Rangeland

8 Oct: KiwiNet Research Commercialisation Awards 2026

15 Oct: Thrive Global Summit

12 Nov: Agritech Unleashed Dunedin

If you have news to share or an opportunity to promote, please contact us and let’s keep building momentum together.

Ngā mihi nui

Brendan O’Connell

Chief Executive, AgriTechNZ

translationZh:
八月份，我们将Bay of Plenty的农业科技社区聚集在Tauranga，举办了Agritech Unleashed活动。创始人、种植者、科技公司、研究人员、投资者和行业领袖齐聚一堂，从第一场会议开始，该地区将创新转化为农场和商业成果的渴望就显而易见。

活动议程的设计是为了引发思考，而非安抚人心。初级产业部（MPI）首席洞察官Jarred Mair开场，探讨了重塑我们农业系统的全球力量。Yamaha Agriculture的Steve Saunders和Sprout Agritech的Dr Sandhya Sriram主持了一场关于在全球范围内建立合作伙伴关系的大师课。工作坊将一天的讨论转化为实际成果，Bioeconomy Science Institute的Kar Mun Chooi探索了数字孪生技术，Rush Digital的Peter McHannigan和Kathryn Mountain则探讨了园艺数据生态系统。

这一天很长，但能量始终充沛，主要是因为人们愿意在同龄人面前说出困难的话。种植者已经停止资助未经证实的技术。可靠性和服务现在决定了什么会被购买。而房间里最初被描述为技术问题的许多事情，结果证明是一个匹配问题：有值得解决的问题的人和有能力解决问题的人，没有足够早地或以足够坦诚的条件找到彼此。

这就是在实地聚集的理由。这些活动不是展示会。它们是行业在一个小到没人能躲在幻灯片后面的房间里检验自身假设的地方，也是关系形成的地方，这些关系在活动结束很久之后仍推动工作向前。在此阅读完整报告。接下来，我们向南进发。11月12日在Dunedin举行的Agritech Unleashed Otago将结束2026年系列活动，以畜牧和牧草系统为背景。问题相同，但答案不会一样。当背景是土地上的动物时，共同进步是什么样子？遗传学、数据、观察和农场决策如何协同而非各自为政？

在前一晚的社交活动拉开序幕后，我们希望你们中的一些人能提前加入我们。我们期待看到生态系统为我们今年的最后一场活动聚集在一起。为此，我们正在与澳大利亚、科罗拉多和怀俄明的合作伙伴一起举办一个关于牧场和草原系统的三部分国际网络研讨会系列……一些全球背景来启发本地洞察。更多内容见下文。

**新国际网络研讨会系列：牧场和草原系统的全球创新**

AgriTech New Zealand正在与澳大利亚、科罗拉多和怀俄明的合作伙伴联合举办一个三部分系列研讨会，探讨创新如何加强牧场和草原系统。

四个地区，四套约束条件，以及大量共同点。农民、牧场主、农业科技领袖、研究人员、投资者和区域发展组织将务实地讨论什么在起作用、什么不起作用：农场韧性、技术采用/适应、投资、政策，以及将 promising 想法推向试点阶段之后所需的合作伙伴关系。

这些会议免费，从九月下旬持续到十月下旬。它们也是为Dunedin活动的有意准备。这里提出的关于放牧系统、数据、采用和生态系统动态的问题，将是我们在十一月舞台上提出的问题，届时将受益于与近邻的国际视角。

每场网络研讨会都包括现场观众问答环节。注册时，您可以提交一个关于塑造牧场和草原系统的挑战、创新或合作机会的紧迫问题。这些问题将帮助引导讨论，并向我们展示更强大的国际联系和共享学习可以在哪里带来实际的下一步。准备好，提出您的问题！

在此注册。

**evokeAG 2027：登记您的意向**

澳大利亚是许多新西兰农业科技公司的天然下一个市场，evokeAG汇聚了可以帮助实现这一转变的人：来自亚太地区的农业企业领袖、政府机构、初创企业、研究人员、生产者和投资者。

它也不仅仅是一个市场。气候压力和客户是整个地区共享的，与新加坡等邻国，关系更加深厚：他们的粮食安全需求与我们的创新能力相互依赖。再加上该地区更好的资本流动，有充分理由制定共同立场，而不是各自为政。

作为该地区最大的农业食品科技活动，evokeAG在两天内汇聚了1500多人。加入新西兰代表团是建立联系、知名度和进入并发展澳大利亚市场所需本地理解的实际方式。

登记加入新西兰代表团（由Sprout Agritech、National Fieldays Society和NZTE联合召集）的意向。参与者将获得：

国际活动门票折扣

协调支持和实地热情介绍

与相关政府机构的联系

通过AgriFutures的GrowAG平台在活动前后获得曝光

在此登记加入代表团的意向。

**年度会议回顾：欢迎我们的新执行委员会**

感谢所有参加8月13日年度会议的人。除了年度回顾和财务报告外，成员们选举产生了新一届执行委员会。委员会设定我们的方向并承载会员的声音，因此值得正式介绍他们。

祝贺Chelsea Hirst（NZ Product Accelerator）和Grant Kay（LIC），他们在选举后加入执行委员会。今年我们在各个类别中再次拥有强大的候选人阵容，以及一场真正有竞争的投票……可能是十一月的热身！对于一个行业组织来说，这是一个好问题。

感谢Tammy Lemire（Pamu）和Elliot Mercer（Agnition），他们在慷慨贡献了时间、人脉和判断力后卸任。两人离开时组织比他们接手时更好，我们期待保持联系。未来一年的执行委员会：

大型企业：Grant Kay（LIC）、Tui Williams（Fonterra）

其他企业：Chelsea Hirst，副主席（NZ Product Accelerator）、Tom Woutersen（Halter）

初创企业和中小企业：Brenna Townshend，主席（Trev）、Sophie Stanley（Levno）

政府：Chris Kerr（MPI）

独立：Ruth Leary（AgriZero）

这里的类别很重要。委员会成员被选举代表一部分会员，而不是他们雇主组织的利益。大型企业席位带来我们会员中每个大型农业企业的视角，初创企业席位代表整个早期阶段公司群体，而不仅仅是他们自己的。这对人们来说是真正的要求，我们的委员会成员认真对待。

这就是我们力量的来源。这八个人在会议之间所做的工作，以及他们背后会员的广度，赋予我们代表行业发言时的地位。只有会员继续举手，这才能维持。感谢你们继续这样做。

**会员聚焦：Macso庆祝五周年**

祝贺MACSO，它刚刚庆祝了五岁生日。MACSO以通过AI变革动物健康的雄心壮志创立，现在正从突破性技术转向全球规模的商业部署。

这一里程碑反映了MACSO团队、客户、合作伙伴、投资者、顾问和支持者的贡献。随着公司进入下一篇章，其进展是新西兰农业科技将雄心勃勃的创新转化为国际影响力的有力例证。

**人事动态**

目前行业中有一个安静的信号，说明了我们走到了哪里。已经证明产品的创始人正在引入高级运营人员来帮助他们扩张，而且做得足够早以产生作用。

在Bovonic，创始人Liam Kampshof及其董事会任命Chris Morgan为总经理，为一家从证明技术转向大规模销售的公司带来了40多年新西兰乳制品行业经验。

在Agovor，联合创始人Richard Beaumont和Simon Carroll让Michael Riley担任CEO，他是一位经验丰富的农业科技运营者，在澳大利亚和新西兰拥有扩张和治理经验。

不同的公司，不同的技术，相同的直觉。将产品推向市场的技能不一定是扩张企业的技能，两组创始人都去寻找做过这件事的人。这既是信心也是雄心的标志。

这也说明了行业的吸引力。有选择权的经验丰富的运营者正在选择农业科技，并选择在这里。人才吸引人才，每一次任命都让下一次更容易实现。祝贺Liam、Richard和Simon，欢迎Chris和Michael。

**即将举行的活动**

9月22日：World Agri-Tech Innovation Summit 2026

9月23-25日：Emergent Leaders for Change Programme

9月28-29日：Red Meat Sector Conference

9月29日：International Webinar Series: Global Innovation in Pasture and Rangeland

10月8日：KiwiNet Research Commercialisation Awards 2026

10月15日：Thrive Global Summit

11月12日：Agritech Unleashed Dunedin

如果您有新闻要分享或机会要推广，请联系我们，让我们一起继续建立势头。

Ngā mihi nui

Brendan O'Connell

首席执行官，AgriTechNZ
